msg: Ultra on root: The tm_dot_prod loop dominates (95.7% of instructions), executing 8 loads, 8 multiplies, and 7 adds per 8-element iteration. The critical path is the multiply-accumulate chain (mul 5-6 cycles + add 3 cycles) which limits ILP throughput to ~1 element/cycle. Loads (lb, 5 cycles) are also frequent but can be overlapped. The 4-byte alignment of inputs enables 32-bit word loads (lw) to replace 4x lb.

proposal.title: 4-element int8 dot product to int32
proposal.rationale: Replaces 4 mul + 3 add + 4 lb with 1 lw + 1 dot4 per 4 elements. Two dot4 + 1 add per 8-element chunk. Eliminates 14 ALU ops and 6 load ops per iteration. Critical path shrinks from 8-cycle mul-add chain to 5-7 cycle dot4 latency. Expected 3.5x fewer cycles in dot product (95.7% of region). Area: 4x 8x8 signed multipliers (4 DSP9x9) + 3 adders ~700 LUT-equiv (27% budget) — may exceed 5% but highest impact.

proposal.title: 2-element int8 dot product with 32-bit accumulate
proposal.rationale: Fuses 2 mul + 2 add + accumulator update into 1 instruction. rs1 holds running sum, rs2 packs 2 sptr + 2 kptr bytes. Per 8 elements: 4 lw (2 sptr, 2 kptr), 4 pack (shift/or), 4 dot2acc. Saves 8 mul + 8 add instructions; pack overhead ~8 ALU ops. Net ~40% instruction reduction in hot loop. Area: 2x 8x8 multipliers (2 DSP9x9) + 2 adders ~300 LUT-equiv (12% budget).

proposal.title: Packed 2x int8 multiply to 2x int16
proposal.rationale: Replaces 2 mul with 1 pmul2, leaving adds to software. Per 8 elements: 4 pmul2 + 6 add (vs 8 mul + 7 add). Saves 4 mul instructions (5-6 cycles each) but adds remain. Loads unchanged (8 lb or 2 lw + extract). ~20% instruction reduction in hot loop. Area: 2x 8x8 multipliers (2 DSP9x9) + packing logic ~150 LUT-equiv (6% budget) — closest to 5% limit.

detail: The dot4 instruction uses four 8×8 signed multipliers (mapping to four DSP9X9 blocks) and three adders, fitting within the area budget while delivering a 3‑5× speedup for inner‑product loops.
pmul2 replaces two int8×int8 multiplies with one custom instruction, saving ~4 mul instructions per 8‑element dot product while adding negligible overhead.
